To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an effective method to learn mid level attribute feature for pedestrian attribute recognition and localization.

the proposed method can learn a set of mid-level feature maps for pedestrian attribute recognition and localization in a weakly-supervised way, and the proposed method can be used for attribute recognition and localization on both the PETA dataset (PETA-attribute) and the RAP Dataset.
the proposed method can be used to localize the locations of pedestrian attributes with the help of mid level attribute feature discovery, which can be achieved in a weakly-supervised manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of weakly supervised learning of mid level features for pedestrian attribute recognition and localization.
the problem of pedestrian attribute recognition and localization, which is of great significance to pedestrian attribute detection, pedestrian re-identification and human behavior understanding.
a novel framework of weakly supervised attribute learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proposed method can achieve competitive attribute recognition accuracy with the state of the art, while also providing the location information of pedestrian attributes, which has not been addressed in previous work.

the method has achieved a promising performance both on attribute recognition and localization, compared to the state of the art, while it is more efficient than previous methods in that it does not require the expensive annotation of attribute bounding boxes.
our method has achieved state of the art performance on attribute recognition and localization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully formulated pedestrian attribute recognition as weakly supervised attribute localizaiton problem and achieved promising results on both recognition and localization.
, we have proposed a weakly supervised framework to jointly learn pedestrian attribute recognition and localization.
we have developed an attribute localization method, which can recognize and localize pedestrian attributes in a weakly labeled manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mid level features can be learned from only image level labels and the location information of pedestrian attributes can also be effectively inferred from these mid level features.
the mid level features are crucial for pedestrian attribute recognition and localization, which is also verified by the results of ablation studies.

the proposed attribute localization approach is able to learn the mid level attribute features in a weakly supervision manner and the learned features are able to capture the spatial distribution information of attributes.
